questions.question: Alcohol in any concentration is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down nerve impulses and body functions. This reduces your control and makes it harder to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as for normal traffic violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Only slow down if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for highway equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever poor visibility makes it hard to see other vehicles. Other drivers also need to see you.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your insurance proof and license to an officer when asked after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. You should:

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if you can.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries or deaths, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can do so safely.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Mirrors on both sides eliminate blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots, and other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, you should:

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and shift to park.
Point your front wheels straight if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and shift to park.
questions.explanation: When parking on a hill, always use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park. If there is no curb, turn your wheels so the car rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. If there is a curb, point wheels toward it (downhill) or slightly away from it (uphill).

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at 55 mph.
The maximum speed limit in good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed for that road. You can drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, it is safe to move back to the right lane when:

options.text: About three seconds have passed.
You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing a vehicle on the left, move back to the right lane when you can see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes poor judgment and slows your reactions. When fatigued, you may fall asleep at the wheel and crash, which can injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not use the full lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Be entirely in the left lane before you start passing and stay there during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be entirely in the left lane before you start passing and stay there during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Do not share the lane. Moving back to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind or partially blind pedestrian. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what laws they must follow. These laws may be about traffic direction, lane use, turns, speed, parking, or special situations. Regulatory signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Immediately enter the right lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up and enter only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you find a gap in traffic. Stay stopped while waiting for a gap to appear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean construction is ahead. Drive with caution.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster. Reduce speed for curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Making a right turn here is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, your tires can lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: What is the law about posters and signs on car windows?

options.text: They are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
They are illegal if they block the driver's view of the road.
They are allowed if they don't contain offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are illegal if they block the driver's view of the road.
questions.explanation: State law prohibits anything on windows that blocks the driver's clear view of the road. No sign, poster, or other material can be placed on a vehicle window if it obstructs the driver's view.

questions.question: When weather or light conditions require you to use headlights, which should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beam light reflects back and creates glare, making it harder to see ahead.

questions.question: What does a dashed white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed lines mean drivers can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Drive carefully and don't slow down to look at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and don't slow down to look at the construction.
questions.explanation: Don't slow down to look at unusual things like construction work. This causes traffic delays.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what does this mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means turns in the direction of the arrow are not allowed. In this case, right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in that direction.
Drivers can turn in that direction after a complete stop.
Drivers can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means traffic cannot proceed in that direction. Drivers must stop and wait for a green signal.
